newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo speeds up output of new video game player.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo speeds up output of new video game player.

text.p: Video game giant Nintendo Co. Ltd, building on the runaway success of its new 64-bit video game player in the United States, is boosting output of the machine ahead of its launch in Europe.

The move, disclosed by managing director Hiroshi Imanishi in an interview with Reuters, comes a week after archrival Sega Enterprises Ltd said it would merge with toymaker Bandai Co. Ltd to become what it called "a formidable force" in the media entertainment business.
Nintendo at the time dismissed the alliance as posing "no worries" for its own business.
Now Nintendo plans to ratchet up shipments of its Nintendo 64 to a million units a month from 700,000 to meet booming demand in the highly competitive U.S. market and a forthcoming launch in Europe,

The Nintendo 64 has sold like hot cakes since it was introduced in Japan in June and in the United States in September, with total shipments reaching 3.99 million units by the end of 1996. Shipments to the U.S. market were 2.14 million.
